business_problem: Fluid Attacks needed to compete with larger cybersecurity providers while keeping infrastructure costs low enough to keep investing in research, talent, and product innovation.
solution_summary: Fluid Attacks runs its infrastructure and technology stack on AWS and used AWS Graviton-based compute plus Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to lower the cost of operating its cybersecurity platform. By moving price-sensitive workloads onto AWS Graviton Processors and flexible EC2 purchase models, the company created a more scalable compute foundation without tying up budget in expensive hardware or overprovisioned capacity. This is especially important for a smaller vendor in a fast-moving market, where savings on the platform can be redirected into the research lab, engineering team, and new security offerings. The result is a cloud architecture optimized for both elasticity and cost discipline: compute remains available on demand, the company can scale rapidly as needed, and the savings become a direct enabler of product development and business growth.

solution_components.name: AWS Graviton Processors
solution_components.role: Provide lower-cost compute for Fluid Attacks' cloud workloads.

solution_components.name: Amazon EC2
solution_components.role: Runs the core cloud infrastructure for Fluid Attacks' platform.

solution_components.name: Amazon EC2 Spot Instances
solution_components.role: Supplies discounted elastic capacity that helps lower operating costs further.

data_flow: Fluid Attacks deploys its platform workloads onto Amazon EC2 using AWS Graviton-based capacity and Spot Instances, creating a lower-cost compute path that keeps the service scalable while freeing budget for R&D and new security capabilities.
business_outcome: Fluid Attacks achieved 70 percent cost savings, can compete more effectively with larger market players, and reinvests the savings into its research lab, team, and innovative customer solutions.

Uses both architecture choice (Graviton) and purchase model (Spot) for savings.
